$comment: Trusted seed list. seedInclusionTypes is authoritative; the classifier still runs for themes and to measure agreement. Sourced from LOC Latinx filmography, UCLA Chicano/Latino TV guide, and editorial curation. Before adding a title, see CRITERIA.md in this directory for the verification checklist. Removing one? List it in `removed` with a reason - CI rejects a title that disappears otherwise.

titles.note: Exception: Spanish director (Icíar Bollaín), but powerfully centers Bolivian indigenous community fight for water rights during 2000 Cochabamba Water War

titles.title: McFarland, USA
titles.note: Exception: Non-Latino director (Niki Caro), but powerfully centers Latino community story and experiences

titles.title: Pan's Labyrinth
titles.note: Exception: Spanish Civil War setting, but Latino (Mexican) director; film centers magical realism (Latin American literary tradition)

titles.ref: Bingo: The King of the Mornings (2017)
titles.title: Bingo: The King of the Mornings
Sin Nombre
titles.note: Exception: Non-Latino director (Cary Joji Fukunaga), but executive producers Diego Luna and Gael García Bernal (Mexican); authentic, critically acclaimed debut; praised for insightful portrayal of Central American migration and gang violence

titles.ref: John Leguizamo's Latin History for Morons (2018)
titles.title: John Leguizamo's Latin History for Morons
Valeria
titles.note: Spain production (Netflix, 4 seasons). starring verified: Diana Gómez (title role) born Igualada, Barcelona (TMDB). led_by/created_by pending (rule #6): developer/S1 writer María López Castaño's heritage has no source yet (TMDB bio empty, no Wikipedia page); episode director Nely Reguera is Spanish (es.wikipedia) but directed 3 episodes, not primary control. No about_community (rule #4). tmdbId pinned - TMDB also has an unrelated 2008 series 'Valeria'.

titles.title: El patrullero 777
titles.note: Director Miguel M. Delgado and star/story writer Cantinflas (Mario Moreno) both born in Mexico City (es.wikipedia). created_by = Cantinflas's story credit (TMDB). about_community left for review: Mexico City police satire - culturally rooted, but uncertain under rule #4 (rule #6).

titles.title: The Little Priest
titles.note: Original title El padrecito (TMDB original_title, already searchable). Director and screenwriter Miguel M. Delgado, star Cantinflas - both born in Mexico City (es.wikipedia). about_community left for review: centers a small Mexican town's church, fiesta and bullfight - arguably qualifies under rule #4, left out as uncertain (rule #6).

titles.ref: Dora and the Search for Sol Dorado (2025)
titles.title: Dora and the Search for Sol Dorado
titles.note: Director Alberto Belli born in Mexico (TMDB person 1544795); Samantha Lorraine (Dora, title role) born to a Cuban family in Los Angeles (en.wikipedia). No created_by: writer JT Billings unverified. about_community left for review: Latina heroine, bilingual, abuela, Colombian Amazon setting - but a treasure-hunt plot (rule #6).

titles.title: The Battle of Chile
titles.note: Patricio Guzmán's three-part documentary on Pinochet's 1973 coup; landmark of political cinema and collective memory

titles.title: The Wolf House
titles.note: Directed by Chilean artists Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña (original title La casa lobo); stop-motion horror fable inspired by Colonia Dignidad, the German sect in Chile tied to the Pinochet regime

titles.title: Zama
titles.note: Lucrecia Martel's colonial historical film; regional influence and aesthetic innovation in contemporary Argentine cinema

titles.title: The Strategy of the Snail
titles.note: Sergio Cabrera's examination of urban inequality and class struggle in Bogotá

titles.title: La vendedora de rosas
titles.note: Víctor Gaviria's portrait of urban street children, gender, and precarity in Medellín

titles.title: Birds of Passage
titles.note: Cristina Gallego & Ciro Guerra's examination of armed conflict and regional Wayuu Indigenous identity

titles.title: Monos
titles.note: Alejandro Landes's intimate portrait of young guerrilla fighters in Colombian armed conflict

titles.title: Mexico 86
titles.note: Gabriel Ripstein (Mexican; son of Arturo Ripstein) directed and co-wrote with Daniel Krauze; Diego Luna as the official who won Mexico the 1986 World Cup. Not César Díaz's 2024 Guatemalan-exile drama of the same name (TMDB 1174027)

titles.title: Goal!
titles.note: Director Danny Cannon and writers Dick Clement & Ian La Frenais are British - no led_by/created_by. Kuno Becker (Mexican) leads as Santiago Muñez, an undocumented Mexican immigrant from LA's barrio; about_community is an editorial call on the immigrant arc framing the story

titles.ref: One, the Story of a Goal (2010)
titles.title: One, the Story of a Goal
titles.note: Documentary co-directed by Gerardo Muyshondt (Salvadoran) and Carlos Moreno (Colombian): El Salvador's 1982 World Cup team, qualifying at the start of the civil war

titles.title: Limite
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #227's merge). Mário Peixoto (Brazilian) wrote and directed. breakthrough: voted #1 in Abraccine's 2015 Top 100 Brazilian films. No about_community - an abstract film about three people adrift at sea

titles.title: Terra em Transe
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #227's merge; never ingested - TMDB lists it as Entranced Earth). Glauber Rocha (Brazilian) wrote and directed; Cinema Novo allegory of Latin American political crisis

titles.title: Pixote
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #227's merge). Héctor Babenco (Argentine-born Brazilian) directed and co-wrote; São Paulo street children

titles.title: Los olvidados
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #229's merge) and pinned: title search had matched a 2014 film of the same name. Luis Buñuel (Spanish, naturalized Mexican) directed and co-wrote; Mexico City street children. breakthrough: original negative inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register (2003)

titles.title: The Exterminating Angel
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #229's merge). Buñuel directed and co-wrote. No about_community - a universal allegory of a trapped bourgeois dinner party

titles.title: Canoa
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #229's merge; never ingested - TMDB lists it as Canoa: A Shameful Memory). Felipe Cazals (Mexican) directed; the 1968 San Miguel Canoa lynching

titles.title: Rojo amanecer
titles.note: Restored (dropped by #229's merge; never ingested). Jorge Fons (Mexican) directed; the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre

removed.reason: No 1977 film could be confirmed to exist (CRITERIA rule 6); TMDB title search only matched a 1910 silent film, which went live as manuel-rodriguez-1910
